subject.title: sessions_spawn from a CLI-harness parent (claude-cli) clamps subagents to gateway bridge tools — children lose exec/read/write

question: For CLI-harness parent sessions, should subagent tool inheritance use the parent harness's native file/shell capability instead of the OpenClaw bridge-visible tool list, and which explicit restrictions must still be inherited?
rationale: The bug path is clear, but deciding how to avoid privilege escalation across native CLI harnesses is a security-boundary policy choice rather than a safe blind repair.

options.title: Add native-capability inheritance
options.body: Model CLI-harness native file/shell capability as a prepared fact and inherit that for child allowlists while preserving explicit denies and real restrictive config policies.

options.title: Exempt bridge-only allowlists
options.body: Do not capture runtime bridge allowlists from native CLI parents, which is simpler but may miss future harnesses with genuinely narrower native capability.

options.title: Add an operator switch
options.body: Expose inheritance mode as config, which gives operators control but adds new surface in an already security-sensitive tool-policy area.

recommendation.title: Add native-capability inheritance
recommendation.body: Model CLI-harness native file/shell capability as a prepared fact and inherit that for child allowlists while preserving explicit denies and real restrictive config policies.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest routing candidate because the decision spans Agents and Security ownership and current work on the exact tool-policy files.
